messages:
Maria (People Ops): kicking off the vendor migration checklist — quick q's before we share comms. who owns the withholding switch date for active employees vs contractors?
Kevin (Payroll): payroll team owns mapping but need confirmation from benefits on plan IDs and effective date. payroll can only change deduction codes at payroll cutoff.
Sophie (Benefits): plan IDs ready. new vendor uses PID-RED-2026 for core 401k and PID-RED-2026-R for Roth. recommended effective date is first pay period after 5/15. that gives 2 payroll cycles for mapping.
Maria (People Ops): OK — so employees who submit deferral changes between now and cutoff — do we honor old elections for that pay or the new?
Kevin (Payroll): operationally we honor the election tied to the payroll run. if change received before the cutoff for that run -> apply. after cutoff -> next run.
Ellen (HRIS): shortlist: need CSV with employee sid, old plan code, new plan code, deferral percent, pre-tax vs roth flag, catch-up indicator, and loan status. I can accept that format.
Sophie (Benefits): note: catch-up (age 50+) contributions need carry-forward flags. vendor expects a separate field 'catch_up_flag' = Y/N. also vendor does not automatically convert legacy pre-tax catch-up entries — we'll need manual mapping for any special cases.
Tim (Finance): what about outstanding 401k loans? will vendor import balances or will we run a separate loan-transfer?
Sophie (Benefits): vendor can import loan balances but requires amortization schedule CSV. if we can't provide that, loans remain on legacy record and repayments continue via payroll to old plan until full payoff — messy. prefer full import.
Kevin (Payroll): can we produce amort schedules? our payroll system stores original loan amount, start date, payment amount, term, and remaining balance. Ellen, can you export loan schedule fields by next Tue?
Ellen (HRIS): yes, I'll pull and validate identifiers. will need sample mapping first.
Maria (People Ops): what about employees currently in mid-cycle distribution or hardship requests?
Sophie (Benefits): distributions in-flight should be paid from legacy vendor. we must set a blackout window for new distribution submission during cutover — recommend 48 hours before final payroll cut. communicate that clearly.
Payroll Bot: Reminder: payroll cutoff for payperiod ending 5/12 is 2026-05-10 18:00 UTC. Any deduction code changes after that will apply to next pay date.
Kevin (Payroll): noted — timeline looks like: finalize mapping CSV by 5/5, loan schedules by 5/7, trial import and reconcile 5/8-5/12, stop distribution submissions 5/10, go-live for deductions 5/15 pay date.
Maria (People Ops): communications question — for people on variable pay (commissions, contractors) do we auto-enroll them into the new vendor or leave as-is?
Sophie (Benefits): contractors are non-eligible for our 401k; they won't be migrated. variable comp employees with eligibility should be migrated but we need to check pay codes so deferrals hit correctly.
Tim (Finance): also flag employees with mid-year promotion that changes eligibility tier — they need manual review so they don't get double deductions.
Ellen (HRIS): I'll add a 'manual review' column to the export and tag anyone with recent status change in the last 60 days.
Maria (People Ops): awesome. last: if an employee is trying to do a Roth in-plan conversion during the cutover window, do we allow it?
Sophie (Benefits): recommend blocking in-plan conversions 7 days before and 7 days after go-live to avoid reconciliation issues. include instructions for submitting a request after the blackout.
Maria (People Ops): perfect. I'll draft the employee comms and the internal checklist. action owners: Ellen = exports by 5/5, Kevin = payroll mapping and test import, Sophie = vendor liaison and blackout schedule, Tim = finance sign-off on loan import. will post draft comms later today. :raised_hands:
